# Loading data

## Overview

The `ems_data()` function loads and prepares GTAP database files for use in CGE model runs.
It handles the three core GTAP data files (dat, par, and set) and is also used to specify any time steps (for temporally dynamic models) and load set mappings for sets that are read into the model (i.e., not constructed from set operations).

```r
ems_data(
  dat_input,
  par_input,
  set_input,
  time_steps = NULL,
  ...
)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `dat_input` | Character or list | Path to a HAR file containing basedata coefficient data, or a `dat` list from [`GTAP_convert()`](#converting-formats) |
| `par_input` | Character or list | Path to a HAR file containing parameter coefficient data, or a `par` list from [`GTAP_convert()`](#converting-formats) |
| `set_input` | Character or list | Path to a HAR file containing set elements and attributes, or a `set` list from [`GTAP_convert()`](#converting-formats) |
| `time_steps` | Integer vector or `NULL` | Time steps for intertemporal models (see [Time steps]) |
| `...` | Named arguments | Set mappings for read-in sets (see [Loading and specifying sets](set_mappings.qmd)) |

All three input files (`dat_input`, `par_input`, `set_input`) and model-specific set mappings are required.
`time_steps` is required for intertemporal models.

## Input files
Compatible input files are currently limited to those produced by the Global Trade Analysis Project [(GTAP)](https://www.gtap.agecon.purdue.edu/).
Although the most recent database releases are proprietary, GTAP has consistently made databases publicly available two versions behind the current release (GTAP 10 as of the current GTAP 12 release).

In order to access the freely available database, users will need to [register](https://www.gtap.agecon.purdue.edu/access_member/profile/profile_addnew.aspx) with GTAP and download the "FlexAgg" format.
For GTAP 10 this is accessible under the "GDyn Data Base" entry in the GTAP 10 "Satellite Data and Utilities" section [here](https://www.gtap.agecon.purdue.edu/securedFile/Filedownload.aspx?fileid=1317).
For paying GTAP members, the current [`teems`](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-R) version is capable of handling the "FlexAgg" format for GTAP Databases Version 9 and above.

The following command will load data consistent with the [standard GTAP model](https://www.gtap.agecon.purdue.edu/resources/res_display.asp?RecordID=6438), using broad aggregations for regions, commodities, and endowments.
Users will need to specify the location of data (`"v7_data/gsdfdat.har"` placeholder).

```r
v7_data <- ems_data(dat_input = "v7_data/gsdfdat.har", # basedata coefficients
                    par_input = "v7_data/gsdfpar.har", # parameter coefficients
                    set_input = "v7_data/gsdfset.har", # set elements
                    REG = "big3",
                    ACTS = "macro_sector",
                    ENDW = "labor_diff"
)
```

Note that the actual names of HAR data files vary according to the GTAP release.

A database held in a single HAR file, such as the ORANI-G `basedata.har`, is loaded by giving `dat_input` alone.
Every character header with distinct entries becomes a set named after its header, every real header a coefficient dimensioned by the set labels stored in the file, and the data are passed through at full resolution; set mappings do not apply on this route.

```r
orani_data <- ems_data(dat_input = "oranig/basedata.har")
```

Sets read this way keep the element order of their header in the file, as in GEMPACK; so does any set passed through without aggregation on the GTAP route.
Aggregated sets are ordered by their mapping.
The order matters to a model that works by position, for example through `$POS` or a mapping read from a header.

A real header stored without set labels is laid out over the sets declared by the coefficient that reads it, in the file's storage order.
If the header's size or shape does not fit that declaration, [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd) stops with an error naming the header and the coefficient.

| Input Type | GTAP v9 | GTAP v10 | GTAP v11 | GTAP v12 |
|------------|---------|----------|----------|----------|
| dat_input  | gddat.har | gsddat.har | gsdfdat.har | gsdfdat.har |
| par_input  | gdpar.har | gsdpar.har | gsdfpar.har | gsdfpar.har |
| set_input  | gdset.har | gsdset.har | gsdfset.har | gsdfset.har |


## Set mappings

Set mappings aggregate the fine-grained regions, sectors, and endowments in the GTAP database down to the resolution required for a given model run.
The set names used in `...` depend on the data format — see the [Loading and specifying sets](set_mappings.qmd) chapter for the full list of internal mappings and instructions for supplying custom CSV mappings.

## Time steps
For temporally dynamic models (e.g., [GTAP-RE](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-models/tree/main/GTAP-RE)), time steps must be provided representing t0 plus actual year steps from t0.
Time steps can be inputted in either actual year increments or represented as chronological years.
Note that if chronological years are used, t0 must correspond with the reference year of the database being used.

The following uses explicit time steps (steps from t0), equivalent to chronological years `c(2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2023, 2025, 2027, 2029, 2031, 2033)` for a database with a 2017 reference year.
```r
data <- ems_data(dat_input = "v7_data/gsdfdat.har",
                 par_input = "v7_data/gsdfpar.har",
                 set_input = "v7_data/gsdfset.har",
                 time_steps = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16),
                 REG = "WB23",
                 ACTS = "services",
                 ENDW = "labor_agg"
)
```

Chronological time steps (with t0 corresponding to the reference year of input data).
```r
data <- ems_data(dat_input = "v7_data/gsdfdat.har",
                 par_input = "v7_data/gsdfpar.har",
                 set_input = "v7_data/gsdfset.har",
                 time_steps = c(2017, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024, 2026, 2028, 2030),
                 REG = "R32",
                 ACTS = "medium",
                 ENDW = "labor_diff"
)
```
## Converting formats
`GTAP_convert()` reads a GTAP database's HAR files into R at full resolution, without any aggregation, which makes it the easy way to inspect or modify a database.
With `target`, it can also convert a standard GTAP database between the v6.2 and v7 formats, or prepare a GTAP-AEZ, GTAP-E or GTAP-Power database for its model.
The returned list can be passed directly to `ems_data()` or [`ems_example()`](example.qmd).
After a conversion, set mappings are specified for the target format, *not* the original format of the data.

```r
GTAP_convert(
  dat_har,
  par_har,
  set_har,
  target = NULL
)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `dat_har` | Character | Path to the basedata HAR file |
| `par_har` | Character | Path to the parameter HAR file |
| `set_har` | Character | Path to the set HAR file |
| `target` | Character or `NULL` | `NULL` reads the files as they are. `"GTAPv6"` or `"GTAPv7"` converts a standard GTAP database to that format (standard GTAP databases only). `"GTAP-AEZ"`, `"GTAP-E"` or `"GTAP-EP"` prepares that model's database, without converting its format |

### Loading HAR files as arrays

When `target` is omitted, `GTAP_convert()` simply parses the HAR files into lists of arrays:

```r
dat <- GTAP_convert(
  dat_har = "v7_data/gsdfdat.har",
  par_har = "v7_data/gsdfpar.har",
  set_har = "v7_data/gsdfset.har"
)

v7_data <- ems_data(dat_input = dat$dat,
                    par_input = dat$par,
                    set_input = dat$set,
                    REG = "big3",
                    ACTS = "macro_sector",
                    ENDW = "labor_diff"
)
```

### Converting between classic (v6x) and standard (v7x) formats

To use the classic model with a v7-format database, or the standard model with a v6-format database, specify `target`.
Format conversion applies to the standard GTAP database only.

A GTAP 12 database converted to v6.2 format for the classic GTAP model:
```r
converted <- GTAP_convert(
  dat_har = "v7_data/gsdfdat.har",
  par_har = "v7_data/gsdfpar.har",
  set_har = "v7_data/gsdfset.har",
  target = "GTAPv6"
)

v6_data <- ems_data(dat_input = converted$dat,
                    par_input = converted$par,
                    set_input = converted$set,
                    REG = "big3",
                    PROD_COMM = "macro_sector",
                    ENDW_COMM = "labor_agg"
)
```

A GTAP 10 database converted to v7 format for the standard GTAP model:
```r
converted <- GTAP_convert(
  dat_har = "v6_data/gsddat.har",
  par_har = "v6_data/gsdpar.har",
  set_har = "v6_data/gsdset.har",
  target = "GTAPv7"
)

v7_data <- ems_data(dat_input = converted$dat,
                    par_input = converted$par,
                    set_input = converted$set,
                    REG = "AR5",
                    ACTS = "macro_sector",
                    ENDW = "labor_agg"
)
```

### GTAP-AEZ, GTAP-E and GTAP-Power databases

The GTAP-AEZ, GTAP-E and GTAP-EP models read sets and parameters that their databases do not ship in the form the model expects.
`ems_data()` recognises these databases and prepares them on load, so the HAR files can be passed directly.
To work with a prepared database in R before aggregation, use `GTAP_convert()` with `target = "GTAP-AEZ"`, `"GTAP-E"` or `"GTAP-EP"`; this prepares the database (generates new headers) but does not convert its format.
Conversion between v6 and v7 versions of these databases is not supported.

```r
e_data <- ems_data(dat_input = "e_data/gsdfdat.har",
                   par_input = "e_data/gsdfpar.har",
                   set_input = "e_data/gsdfset.har",
                   REG = "big3",
                   ACTS = "energy"
)
```

## Data aggregation
Data is aggregated according to type, with non-parameter coefficients summed by target set mappings and weighted averages calculated for the parameters below.
A simple mean is applied to parameters not listed below, and to the two base data headers that are not values: `DPSM` (the sum of the household distribution parameters, 1 in every region) and, in GTAP-E and GTAP-Power data, `GSHR` (the government share of carbon tax revenue).
If custom parameter values are desired, these can be directly loaded in their final format into the [`ems_model()`](model_load.qmd) function, and no aggregation or modification will take place.
In the below notation, hat (ˆ) indicates the new parameter value and asterisk indicates the destination set mapping.

### Parameter weights
The elasticities are aggregated region by region, so each aggregated region keeps its own values.
Two weighting methods are available through the `par_weights` argument of `ems_data()`:

- `"share"` (default): each member is weighted by the value of its CES or CET nest, $V$, times one minus the sum of its squared input shares $\theta_k$,
$$
w = V\left(1 - \sum_k \theta_k^2\right).
$$
This is the weight under which the aggregate elasticity reproduces the members' response to a small change in relative prices.
A member whose input shares cannot move carries little weight: a commodity that is almost never imported cannot shift the aggregate import share, whatever its elasticity, and neither can imports bought almost entirely from one source.
For a nest with two inputs the weight reduces to $2 V \theta (1 - \theta)$.
Shares are taken over the inputs of the aggregated model (for import sourcing, the aggregated source regions).
Where every member of an aggregate has a zero weight, the value weight is used instead.
- `"value"`: each member is weighted by the value of its nest, as the GTAP aggregation programs (FlexAgg) do for their region-specific parameters; the formulas are given below.

A single method applies to every weighted parameter; individual parameters can be set apart by name:

```r
v7_data <- ems_data("v7_data/gsdfdat.har",
                    "v7_data/gsdfpar.har",
                    "v7_data/gsdfset.har",
                    REG = "big3",
                    ACTS = "macro_sector",
                    ENDW = "labor_agg",
                    par_weights = c(ESBM = "value"))
```

The CDE parameters (INCP, SUBP) are not substitution elasticities and are weighted by private consumption under either method.
The nests behind the share weights:

::: {.table-scroll .table-wide}
| Header | Nest | Inputs ($\theta_k$) | Value ($V$) |
|--------|------|----------------------|-------------|
| ESBD | domestic/imported, one per agent | domestic, imported | purchases by firms, households, government and investment (v6: firms, households, government) |
| ESBM | import sourcing | aggregated source regions | bilateral imports (VMSB; v6 VIMS) |
| ESBV | primary factors | aggregated endowments | factor payments (EVFP; v6 EVFA) |
| ESBT | intermediates/value added | intermediates, value added | intermediate purchases plus factor payments |
| ESBC | intermediate inputs | aggregated commodities | intermediate purchases |
| ESBG | government demand | aggregated commodities | government purchases |
| ESBI | investment demand | aggregated commodities | investment purchases |
| ETRQ | commodities made by an activity (CET) | aggregated commodities | make matrix (MAKS) |
| ESBQ | activities making a commodity | aggregated activities | make matrix (MAKB) |
| ETRE | allocation of an endowment (CET) | aggregated activities | endowment supply (EVOS) |
| EFVE | value added/energy (GTAP-E, GTAP-Power) | value added, energy | factor payments plus energy purchases |
| EAEZ | land across agro-ecological zones (GTAP-AEZ) | aggregated zones | land rents |
:::

ELFVAEN for fossil fuel mining is recalibrated rather than averaged under either method (see below).

### GTAP v6.2 format parameter weight methodology
Headers, descriptions, and index ranges for parameters and associated data within the GTAP v6.2 model, with the `"value"` weights.

::: {.table-scroll .table-wide}
|                        | Header | Description                                          | Set Index                                                                 |
|------------------------|--------|------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Param.**             |        |                                                      |                                                                           |
| $\sigma_\text{d}$      | ESBD   | Armington CES for dom./imp. allocation       | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM}$                                                 |
| $\sigma_\text{m}$      | ESBM   | Armington CES for regional allocation of imports     | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM}$                                                 |
| $\sigma_\text{va}$     | ESBV   | CES between primary factors in production            | $j \in \text{PROD\_COMM}$                                                 |
| $\sigma_\text{t}$      | ESBT   | Elasticity of intermediate input substitution        | $j \in \text{PROD\_COMM}$                                                 |
| $\gamma$               | INCP   | CDE expansion parameter                              | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$                             |
| $\beta$                | SUBP   | CDE substitution parameter                           | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$                             |
| **Data**               |        |                                                      |                                                                           |
|                        | EVFA   | Endowments – Firms purchases at agents' prices       | $i \in \text{ENDW\_COMM},\ j \in \text{PROD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$   |
|                        | VDFA   | Inter. – Firms' dom. purchases at agents' prices | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ j \in \text{PROD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$   |
|                        | VDGA   | Inter. – Government dom. purchases at agents'    | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$                             |
|                        | VDPA   | Inter. – Household dom. purchases at agents'     | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$                             |
|                        | VIFA   | Inter. – Firms' imp. at agents' prices            | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ j \in \text{PROD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$   |
|                        | VIGA   | Inter. – Government imp. at agents' prices        | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$                             |
|                        | VIPA   | Inter. – Household imp. at agents' prices         | $i \in \text{TRAD\_COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$                             |

:::

#### Aggregation methods
$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{d}_i} =
\frac{
\sum_{i}^{i^*}
\left(
\sigma_{\text{d}_i}
\sum_r
(vdpa_{i,r} + vdga_{i,r} + vdfa_{i,r} + vipa_{i,r} + viga_{i,r} + vifa_{i,r})
\right)
}
{
\sum_{i,r}^{i^*}
(vdpa_{i,r} + vdga_{i,r} + vdfa_{i,r} + vipa_{i,r} + viga_{i,r} + vifa_{i,r})
}
$$ {#eq-sigmaD}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{m}_i} =
\frac{
\sum_{i}^{i^*}
\left(
\sigma_{\text{m}_i}
\sum_r
(vipa_{i,r} + viga_{i,r} + vifa_{i,r})
\right)
}
{
\sum_{i,r}^{i^*}
(vipa_{i,r} + viga_{i,r} + vifa_{i,r})
}
$$ {#eq-sigmaM}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{va}_j} =
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\frac{
\sum_{j}^{j^*}
\left(
\sigma_{\text{va}_j}
\sum_r evfa_{j,r}
\right)
}{
\sum_{j,r}^{j^*} evfa_{j,r}
}
& \text{if } j \neq cgds \\
\sigma_{\text{va}_j}
& \text{if } j = cgds
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-sigmaVA}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{t}_j} =
\frac{
\sum_{j}^{j^*}
\left(
\sigma_{\text{t}_j}
\sum_{i,r}
(vdfa_{i,j,r} + vifa_{i,j,r})
\right)
}
{
\sum_{i,j,r}^{j^*}
(vdfa_{i,j,r} + vifa_{i,j,r})
}
$$ {#eq-sigmaT}

$$
\hat{\gamma}_{i,r} =
\frac{
\sum_{i,r}^{i^* r^*}
\gamma_{i,r}
\sum_{i,r} (vdpa_{i,r} + vipa_{i,r})
}{
\sum_{i,r}^{i^* r^*}
(vdpa_{i,r} + vipa_{i,r})
}
$$ {#eq-gamma}

$$
\hat{\beta}_{i,r} =
\frac{
\sum_{i,r}^{i^* r^*}
\left(
\beta_{i,r}
\sum_{i,r} (vdpa_{i,r} + vipa_{i,r})
\right)
}{
\sum_{i,r}^{i^* r^*}
(vdpa_{i,r} + vipa_{i,r})
}
$$ {#eq-beta}

### GTAP v7.1 format parameter weight methodology
Headers, descriptions, and index ranges for parameters and associated data within the GTAP v7 model, with the `"value"` weights.
The same weights apply to the other v7-format models, with GTAP-RE adding an invariant time set.

::: {.table-scroll .table-wide}
|                        | Header | Description                                           | Set Index                                      |
|------------------------|--------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| **Param.**             |        |                                                       |                                                |
| $\sigma_\text{d}$  | ESBD   | Armington CES for domestic/imported allocation        | $c \in \text{COMM}$                            |
| $\sigma_\text{m}$  | ESBM   | Armington CES for regional allocation of imports      | $c \in \text{COMM}$                            |
| $\sigma_\text{va}$ | ESBV   | CES between primary factors in production             | $a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
| $\sigma_\text{t}$  | ESBT   | CES between intermediate inputs and value added       | $a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
| $\sigma_\text{c}$  | ESBC   | CES between intermediate inputs                       | $a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
| $\sigma_\text{g}$  | ESBG   | CES of government demand                              | $r \in \text{REG}$                            |
| $\omega_\text{q}$  | ETRQ   | CET between commodities produced by an activity       | $a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
| $\sigma_\text{q}$  | ESBQ   | CES between activities producing a commodity          | $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
| $\gamma$               | INCP   | CDE expansion parameter                               | $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
| $\beta$                | SUBP   | CDE substitution parameter                            | $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
| **Data**               |        |                                                       |                                                |
|                        | EVFP   | Primary factor purchases at purchasers' prices        | $e \in \text{ENDW},\ a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$ |
|                        | VDFP   | Domestic purchases by firms at purchasers' prices     | $c \in \text{COMM},\ a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$ |
|                        | VDGP   | Domestic purchases by government at purchasers' prices| $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
|                        | VDPP   | Domestic purchases by households at purchasers' prices| $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
|                        | VMFP   | Import purchases by firms at purchasers' prices       | $c \in \text{COMM},\ a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$ |
|                        | VMGP   | Import purchases by government at purchasers' prices  | $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
|                        | VMPP   | Import purchases by households at purchasers' prices  | $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
|                        | VDIP   | Domestic purchases by investment at purchasers' prices| $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
|                        | VMIP   | Import purchases by investment at purchasers' prices  | $c \in \text{COMM},\ r \in \text{REG}$         |
|                        | MAKS   | Make matrix at supply prices                          | $c \in \text{COMM},\ a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$ |
|                        | MAKB   | Make matrix at basic prices                           | $c \in \text{COMM},\ a \in \text{ACTS},\ r \in \text{REG}$ |


:::

#### Aggregation methods
$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{d}_{c}} = \frac{\sum_{c}^{c^{*}}\left(\sigma_{\text{d}_{c}}\sum_{r} (vdpp_{c,r} + vmpp_{c,r} + vdgp_{c,r} + vmgp_{c,r} + vdfp_{c,r} + vmfp_{c,r} + vdip_{c,r} + vmip_{c,r})\right)}
                    {\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}} (vdpp_{c,r} + vmpp_{c,r} + vdgp_{c,r} + vmgp_{c,r} + vdfp_{c,r} + vmfp_{c,r} + vdip_{c,r} + vmip_{c,r})}
$$ {#eq-sigmaD-v7}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{m}_{c}} = \frac{\sum_{c}^{c^{*}}\left(\sigma_{\text{m}_{c}}\sum_{r} (vmpp_{c,r} + vmgp_{c,r} + vmfp_{c,r} + vmip_{c,r})\right)}
      {\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}} (vmpp_{c,r} + vmgp_{c,r} + vmfp_{c,r} + vmip_{c,r})}
$$ {#eq-sigmaM-v7}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{va}_{a}} = \frac{\sum_{a}^{a^{*}}\left(\sigma_{\text{va}_{a}}\sum_{r} evfp_{a,r}\right)}
                               {\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}} evfp_{a,r}}
$$ {#eq-sigmaVA-v7}

$$
\hat{\gamma}_{c,r} = \frac{\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}r^{*}}\gamma_{c,r}\sum_{c,r} (vdpp_{c,r} + vmpp_{c,r})}
      {\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}r^{*}} (vdpp_{c,r} + vmpp_{c,r})}
$$ {#eq-gamma-v7}

$$
\hat{\beta}_{c,r} = \frac{\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}r^{*}}\left(\beta_{c,r}\sum_{c,r} (vdpp_{c,r} + vmpp_{c,r})\right)}
      {\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}r^{*}} (vdpp_{c,r} + vmpp_{c,r})}
$$ {#eq-beta-v7}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{t}_{a,r}} = \frac{\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}}\sigma_{\text{t}_{a,r}}\left(\sum_{c} (vdfp_{c,a,r} + vmfp_{c,a,r}) + \sum_{e} evfp_{e,a,r}\right)}
      {\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}}\left(\sum_{c} (vdfp_{c,a,r} + vmfp_{c,a,r}) + \sum_{e} evfp_{e,a,r}\right)}
$$ {#eq-sigmaT-v7}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{c}_{a,r}} = \frac{\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}}\sigma_{\text{c}_{a,r}}\sum_{c} (vdfp_{c,a,r} + vmfp_{c,a,r})}
      {\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}}\sum_{c} (vdfp_{c,a,r} + vmfp_{c,a,r})}
$$ {#eq-sigmaC-v7}

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{g}_{r}} = \frac{\sum_{r}^{r^{*}}\sigma_{\text{g}_{r}}\sum_{c} (vdgp_{c,r} + vmgp_{c,r})}
      {\sum_{r}^{r^{*}}\sum_{c} (vdgp_{c,r} + vmgp_{c,r})}
$$ {#eq-sigmaG-v7}

$$
\hat{\omega}_{\text{q}_{a,r}} = \frac{\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}}\omega_{\text{q}_{a,r}}\sum_{c} maks_{c,a,r}}
      {\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}}\sum_{c} maks_{c,a,r}}
\qquad
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{q}_{c,r}} = \frac{\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}r^{*}}\sigma_{\text{q}_{c,r}}\sum_{a} makb_{c,a,r}}
      {\sum_{c,r}^{c^{*}r^{*}}\sum_{a} makb_{c,a,r}}
$$ {#eq-sigmaQ-v7}

### GTAP-E, GTAP-Power and GTAP-AEZ parameters
The layer parameters are averaged, except for the following.

The elasticity of substitution between value added and energy, $\sigma_\text{vae}$ (`EFVE`), is weighted by the share weight of the value-added/energy nest (`"share"`) or by the value of primary factors and energy inputs (`"value"`), where $g$ runs over the energy commodities (`COME`):

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{vae}_{a,r}} = \frac{\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}}\sigma_{\text{vae}_{a,r}}\,vaen_{a,r}}{\sum_{a,r}^{a^{*}r^{*}} vaen_{a,r}},
\qquad
vaen_{a,r} = \sum_{e} evfp_{e,a,r} + \sum_{g} (vdfp_{g,a,r} + vmfp_{g,a,r})
$$ {#eq-sigmaVAE}

For the fossil fuel mining activities (coal, oil and gas) it is instead recalibrated at the aggregate level so that the activity reproduces the target supply elasticity $\eta$ (`SPLY`, averaged over all regions), given the cost shares of natural resources ($s_\text{nr}$) and of $vaen$ ($s_\text{vaen}$) in the value of output:

$$
\hat{\sigma}_{\text{vae}_{a,r}} = \frac{\eta_{a}}{1/s_{\text{nr}_{a,r}} - 1/s_{\text{vaen}_{a,r}}}
$$ {#eq-sigmaVAE-fossil}

The other fuels (`p_c`, `gdt`) take $\hat{\sigma}_\text{vae} = 1$.

The elasticity of substitution between land in different agro-ecological zones, $\sigma_\text{aez}$ (`EAEZ`), is weighted by land rents, the primary factor purchases $evfp_{e,a,r}$ over the zones $e \in$ `AEZS` (`"value"`), or by their share weight across zones (`"share"`).
